extracted.intended_audience: Apple customers and device owners seeking repair, replacement, and safety guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Apple product owners (and repair decision-makers) about designing for longevity, obtaining safe repairs, avoiding counterfeit parts, and using Apple service programs and AppleCare coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designing for longevity
rubrics_metrics.description: At Apple, designing for longevity is a company-wide effort informing earliest decisions; it is guided by historical customer-use data and predictions on future usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires striking a balance between durability and repairability while not compromising safety, security, and privacy. Includes making products that last and providing access to safe and reliable repairs (see linked PDF for more detail).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use genuine Apple parts (avoid counterfeit/third‑party parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some counterfeit and third party power adapters and batteries may not be designed properly and could result in safety issues. Non-genuine replacement displays may have compromised visual quality and may fail to work correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure a genuine Apple battery during replacement, visit an Apple Store or Apple Authorized Service Provider. If you need a replacement adapter, Apple recommends getting an Apple power adapter. Apple‑certified screen repairs are performed by trusted experts using genuine Apple parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: AppleCare plan coverage and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Every AppleCare plan provides one-stop service for Apple products, with quick and easy repairs for accidents like drops and spills, and coverage if an iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch is lost or stolen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AppleCare gives centralized service and streamlined support for accidental damage and certain loss/theft scenarios; users should learn more about plan details to understand coverage and repair options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Apple‑certified repair providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple Repair and Service can help you find an Apple‑certified repair performed by trusted experts who use genuine Apple parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer Apple Stores or Apple Authorized Service Providers for repairs to ensure the use of genuine parts and trusted technicians. Start a repair via Apple Repair and Service channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check applicable Apple Service Programs and recalls
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple publishes service programs for known issues (examples listed: Mac mini Service Program for No Power Issue; iPhone 14 Plus Service Program for Rear Camera Issue; 15-inch MacBook Pro Battery Recall Program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you experience a model-specific problem, consult Apple Service Programs / recall pages to see if your device is eligible for a repair, replacement, or recall/notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of scams (e.g., gift card scams)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of scams involving Apple Gift Cards, App Store & iTunes Gift Cards, and Apple Store Gift Cards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apple warns users to be cautious about gift card scams and provides resources/links to learn more about identifying and avoiding such scams.
